digest.component_or_area: LLM provider resolution / model class configuration
propositions: A configured Bedrock provider is silently dropped when the model id contains a colon in its version suffix (canonical form like 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'), causing the model to be treated as unqualified and infer_provider to extract an invalid provider name from the id fragment.

The bug exists because _resolve_target and infer_provider independently scan for ':' to detect provider-qualification, mistakenly treating version colons as separator colons, resulting in two incompatible implementations of the same qualification test.

Guard order is incorrect: the presence of a colon in the model string is checked before an explicitly configured provider is honored, allowing punctuation in the model id to overrule the operator's configuration.

Downstream errors report a fragment of the model id (e.g., 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1') as an invalid provider name, contradicting the operator's actual configuration and making the true cause unguessable.
Only unversioned Bedrock aliases without colons (like 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6') work correctly, masking the bug for the majority of canonical Bedrock ids that AWS publishes.
